frames.narration: An engineer submits an experiment: with 30% errors on 2 of the 10 checkout instances, the failure rate must stay under 50 per thousand requests. The guardrail is 100 per thousand for the whole service, and the engineer's blast-radius limit is 3 instances.

The planner checks the request: 2 targets is within the limit of 3, there is no open incident, no deploy and enough error budget. The baseline over the last hour is 0 failures per thousand, so the experiment may start.
The control plane tells the agents on 2 instances to return errors for 30% of requests. The fault carries a time to live, so the agents would remove it by themselves if they lost contact.
Clients retry once on another instance, so most failures are hidden. The worst reading is 40 failures per thousand, under the 50 of the hypothesis and well under the 100 guardrail.
The faults expire and are removed. The hypothesis held, and the report records the fault window and the graphs. The team now raises the stakes: kill 5 of the 10 instances, with a limit of 5.

Five processes are killed. Until the load balancer notices, requests sent to them fail, and the five survivors can serve only 75 of the 100 requests per tick, so failures jump to 300 per thousand in the first tick.
The watchdog sees 300 per thousand, above its 100 guardrail, in the very first tick. It tells every agent to stop and restore, the processes are restarted, and the experiment is marked aborted.
The report shows the finding: this service cannot lose half its instances, because the survivors have no headroom. The team gets a ticket to add capacity and then repeats the experiment.
